message.content:
Below is a quick‑look table of the **federal public holidays** that create “long weekends” in Canada for the calendar year 2023.  
(If you’re planning trips for a specific province, you’ll want to double‑check the provincial holidays—many provinces have their own holidays such as Family Day, St. Patrick’s Day, etc.)

| Date (2023) | Holiday | Observed (if the day falls on a weekend) | Typical Long Weekend |
|-------------|---------|------------------------------------------|----------------------|
| **Jan 2**   | New Year’s Day (observed) | Monday | **New Year’s Day** (Mon‑Tue) |
| **Apr 7**   | Good Friday | Friday | **Good Friday + Easter Saturday** (Fri‑Sat) |
| **May 22**  | Victoria Day | Monday | **Victoria Day** (Mon‑Tue) |
| **Jul 3**   | Canada Day (observed) | Monday | **Canada Day** (Mon‑Tue) |
| **Sep 4**   | Labour Day | Monday | **Labour Day** (Mon‑Tue) |
| **Oct 9**   | Thanksgiving | Monday | **Thanksgiving** (Mon‑Tue) |
| **Nov 13**  | Remembrance Day (observed) | Monday | **Remembrance Day** (Mon‑Tue) |
| **Dec 25**  | Christmas Day | Monday | **Christmas** (Mon‑Tue) |
| **Dec 26**  | Boxing Day | Tuesday | **Boxing Day** (Tue‑Wed) |

### How to use this list
- **Long weekends** typically involve a holiday falling on a weekday (Mon–Thu) or an observed holiday on a Monday/Tuesday.  
- If a holiday falls on a weekend, it is usually *observed* on the following Monday, creating a 3‑day stretch (e.g., New Year’s Day 2023 fell on Sunday, so the holiday was observed on Monday Jan 2).  
- Some holidays (like Good Friday) already fall on a Friday, giving you a 3‑day weekend (Fri‑Sat‑Sun).  

Feel free to plug these dates into your holiday‑planning app! If you need the provincial holidays for a particular province (e.g., Family Day in Ontario, St. Patricks’ Day in Newfoundland & Labrador), let me know and I can pull those up for you.
